verdict.rationale: ROS 2's official documentation describes first-party client libraries in multiple languages, mainly C++ and Python. These libraries expose ROS's core functionality, offer an idiomatic Python interface, interoperate across languages through shared code generators, are verified at install time, and include programmatic APIs such as the Python bag reader/writer. Several features are C++-only (intra-process communication, composition, managed lifecycles, content filtering), so the SDKs do not have equal depth across languages. Missing for 10: feature parity across the language SDKs, and independent hands-on corroboration that building against the SDKs works smoothly (community reports of dependency hell and a convoluted build system weigh against this).
